## Close record — Gerrit 1980 merged as `b7a4994742`

Patchset 2 earned `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` and was submitted; `b7a4994742` is on
`origin/main` and carries all eight declared files, including the two patchset 1 omitted:
`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` (+15) and `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py` (+169).

All four acceptance criteria are ticked as MET — box state only, no AC prose touched.

### The correction, in one line

`st_size // nlink` is the right figure for **reporting** a share of usage and the wrong figure
as an **increment** of bytes reclaimed. Patchset 1 conflated the two; the fix separates them
into `entry_size` (reporting, plain `st_size`), `exclusive_size` (`st_nlink == 1` — the
increment for both populate and evict, so each inode is added once and subtracted once) and
`distinct_bytes` (each inode once — ground truth for `startup_sweep`).

Left uncorrected this made the original symptom **worse**: `_evict` credited the free-space
watermark loop with bytes that never left the disk, so the pass stops short of its watermark
believing it recovered space it had not. Measured on the new fixture — evicting one of three
sharing entries credited **69,997 bytes while freeing 20,000**.

### Scope: finishing approved scope, not expanding it

Completing the `janitor.py` and `test_snapshot_janitor.py` work was authorised by this
ticket's own certified plan — its `file_impact` declares both, with the reasons `_evict credits
bytes actually freed; startup_sweep dedupes inodes` and `RED->GREEN oracle for shared-entry
eviction accounting`. That is why this landed as a single bug fix at 376+ non-test lines rather
than needing decomposition. Eviction policy, watermark semantics and the tunables are
untouched; only the arithmetic reported to them changed.

### Finding 3 (`bugfix-size-attestation`) — answered, not ignored

The patchset 1 block reported "verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record". True when
cast, already false by the time it was read:

| event | time (UTC) |
| --- | --- |
| review bot cast `LLM-Review -1` | 2026-08-21 07:27:53 |
| plan-review attestation `signed_at` | 2026-08-21 07:43:42 |

Sixteen minutes apart. The 376-line count was verified independently against the patchset 1
file list (9 + 25 + 301 + 17 + 24). The change was **not** decomposed to duck the line floor —
carving up a fix whose size a signed plan already authorises would have been the wrong answer —
and patchset 2 cleared the finding on its own.

### Kill matrix — one survivor, found and closed

Eight mutations, one per independent side. M1–M6 and M8 died immediately. **M7 (populate
credits `entry_size` instead of `exclusive_size`) initially SURVIVED**: every existing
accounting test began with `startup_sweep`, whose authoritative walk laundered any over-credit
made at populate time, so both sides moved in step — the tautology this project has been bitten
by twice. Closed by adding
`test_populating_shared_entries_tracks_real_disk_without_a_sweep`, which never sweeps and also
asserts `sum(entry_size) > on_disk` so its equality is discriminating rather than satisfiable by
any accounting. M7 then died. No remaining survivors and no equivalent-mutant claims.

M8 (`delta_tree` dropping `writes | _unshareable(target_paths)`) was killed twice
independently — once by the structural inode assert, and once with that assert disabled, to
prove the `flock` leg kills on its own rather than riding along.

### Note for the next reader

`rebar review-plan 8386-a512-4815-4e6b --status` now reports `stale-code` (8 dependency files
changed). That is an artefact of the fix having **landed**: the plan was reviewed against a tree
that did not yet contain it. Checked against the reviewed base sha `9b1d2e68` in a throwaway
worktree and the verdict is identical, so it is not local-HEAD drift and not the AC ticks (the
reason cites dependency files, not material). It is a claim-time gate and does not bear on this
close.
